subject.title: fix(plugins): surface oversized-file warnings in doctor migration reads

question: Should doctor preserve the prior ability to migrate large legacy plugin state, or is leaving files above 10 MiB unmigrated with a warning an intentional supported upgrade contract?
rationale: The correct bounded-read implementation depends on the persisted-state recovery promise; code review cannot decide whether an existing user's large legacy state may be intentionally skipped.

options.title: Preserve migration compatibility
options.body: Revise the reader and migration flow so existing large legacy files still have a bounded, recoverable path into canonical plugin state before merge.

options.title: Adopt a strict cap with recovery
options.body: Approve the 10 MiB limit only with explicit doctor remediation, user-facing documentation, and tests covering recovery of the preserved legacy file.

options.title: Pause the hardening change
options.body: Defer this PR until the migration ownership and oversized-state contract are agreed.

recommendation.title: Preserve migration compatibility
recommendation.body: Revise the reader and migration flow so existing large legacy files still have a bounded, recoverable path into canonical plugin state before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-head contributor implemented the affected migration behavior and is the best available routing candidate from the supplied commit history.
